Plutonic Lithics Record Crystal Mush Processes Beneath the Ohakuri Caldera
 
This past semester I had the privilege to study abroad in NZ through the Frontiers Abroad Geology of New Zealand Program and partake in a semester long research project advised by Prof. Sarah Smithies.
Our study focuses on the magmatic system beneath the Ohakuri Caldera, which, together with the Rotorua Caldera, evacuated >245 km3 of rhyolitic magma in the paired Ohakuri and Mamaku eruptions around 240ka.Using petrography and SEM-EDS-BSE, we analyzed 5 plutonic lithic samples from the Ohakuri Caldera in the Taupō Volcanic Zone. Using feldspar and amphibole compositions, we obtained temperature and pressure estimates, respectively. Granophyric texture dominated the majority of samples, in which quartz and feldspars most likely formed simultaneously through a major decompression event, followed by the infilling of interstitial glass. Thermobarometry estimated that plagioclase formed at approximately 890–910 °C. Preliminary Amphibole thermobarometry at least one crystalization event with gedrite forming at ~6–7 km depth. Glass compositions in our samples differ from those reported in previously studied pumice.


Lacustrine Records of Environmental Change in Eastern Glacier National Park

 

This was my first formal research experience under Prof. Kelly MacGregor and my first exposure to geology field work!
In summer 2024, we collected lake sediment cores from several lakes in the Swiftcurrent Valley to examine changes in sedimentation rate and organic content since ~1800 CE. Preliminary results suggest that lake sedimentation rates increase toward the present, with the highest sedimentation rates occurring in down-valley lakes proximal to greater human activity (e.g., roads, trails, and infrastructure). These rates are an order of magnitude greater than Holocene sedimentation rates identified in previous work.Redrock and Swiftcurrent Lakes are deeper and larger (averaging ~6 m and ~10 m deep, respectively), whereas Fishercap Lake is shallow (~1 m deep), impacting hydrologic conditions within the lakes. Changes in sediment sources and hydrologic residence times vary between lakes.

title: Hi!
text:
My name is Delilah Acosta (pronunciation). The pronouns that I use are she/her/hers.
I am an undergraduate student at Macalester College completing a B.A. in Geology. My research interests include geochemistry, petrology, and geothermal systems.
I was born in El Paso, TX. When I was 18, I received a full ride scholarship to attend Macalester College (Go Scots!) through QuestBridge. I am in now a senior planning my next steps after Mac!
I recently found out that I love cooking for my friends! Mexican delicacies are hard to come by when you’re not in Texas and I love sharing these delicious meals with those around me. I am a fan of emo music, gyming, and horror movies.
You can contact me at dacosta@macalester.edu.

This past semstester I had the privilege to study abroad in NZ through the Frontiers Abroad Geology of New Zealnd Program and partake in a semester long research project advised by Prof. Sarah Smithies.
Our study focuses on the magmatic system beneath the Ohakuri Caldera, which, together with the Rotorua Caldera, evacuated >245 km3 of rhyolitic magma in the paired Ohakuri and Mamaku eruptions around 240ka.
Using petrography and SEM-EDS-BSE, we analyzed 5 plutonic lithic samples from the Ohakuri Caldera in the Taupō Volcanic Zone. Additionally, using feldspar and amphibole compositions, we obtained temperature and pressure estimates, respectively. Granophyric texture dominated the majority of our thin sections, in which quartz and feldspars most likely formed simultaneously through a major decompression event, followed by the infilling of interstitial glass. Thermobarometry estimated that plagioclase formed at approximately 890–910 °C. Amphibole geobarometry suggests two major crystallization events, with edenite forming at ~2 km depth and gedrite forming at ~7–8 km depth. Glass compositions in our samples differ from those reported in previously studied samples.
